critique: The delivered result is positive-variance semiparametric efficiency and uniform Wald inference under explicit nuisance-rate, transport-curvature, and relative-variance conditions; it does not provide inference at exact equality. The degeneracy theorem proves only that one unregularized full-tangent Gaussian spectral construction fails at an admissible identity-compression witness, while honest full-parent adaptation remains open. The framing overclaims necessity when it says covariate regularization, a uniform Hilbert–Schmidt tail, and uniform estimation of the regularized Hessian are all necessary: the proofs establish the generic Gaussian-series criterion and failure of the unregularized route, not a necessity theorem covering every regularized spectral calibration. The claimed phase boundaries are sufficient for the chosen finite-net/DML construction and have no converse, as the note ultimately acknowledges.
